---

# 1. Category Purpose

Category 14 gives the future AI Companion a bounded way to compose two or more
already valid compatible results, or to order already valid groups/results. It
distinguishes a request to compare, rank, find an extremum, take a finite top
or bottom selection, describe a relative change, or use a named baseline from
the metric, dimension, predicate, date, and context language that supplies
its inputs.

Every comparison must retain its left/right or baseline/candidate definitions,
the identical compatible authorized population contract, metric definition and
units, gross/net and fee treatment where money is involved, recorded-currency
partition or separately authorized conversion contract, time/event basis,
grouping definition, values, absolute difference, percentage difference only
where a non-zero meaningful denominator is explicitly valid, sample counts,
coverage, and limitations. Every ranking must retain the selected metric,
direction, eligible population, grouping, exact unrounded sort value,
deterministic tie order, requested and returned limit, and coverage.

This category owns comparison/ranking composition language only. It does not
define a metric or its formula, select a dimension or group, resolve a date,
define an operator, create a cohort/baseline, infer a causal explanation or
trading advice, or choose an untrusted conversation/UI selection.

---

# 2. Category Boundaries

## Included

The exact controlling source vocabulary covers, in source order:

- ranking terms: `best`, `worst`, `top`, `bottom`, `most profitable`, `least
  profitable`, `biggest`, `smallest`, `most consistent`, `most frequent`,
  `most costly`, `highest win rate`, and `lowest expectancy`;
- comparative forms: `better than`, `worse than`, `improved`, `declined`,
  `more profitable`, `less consistent`, `larger losses`, `smaller positions`,
  `higher frequency`, `before versus after`, `current versus previous`,
  `selected trade versus similar trades`, `one ticker versus all other
  tickers`, `tagged versus untagged`, and `followed rule versus broke rule`;
  and
- the `superlative and extremum questions` family.

Shared planning semantics cover explicit metric and basis selection; exact
sort direction; finite top/bottom-N limits; percentile and relative/baseline
claims only under an explicit approved denominator/population; deterministic
ties; no-selection handling; compatible partitions; coverage; authorization;
privacy; and clarification instead of invented inputs.

## Excluded

- Primary intent selection, protected-action confirmation, writes, and
  mutation authorization: Category 1.
- Metric formula, units, fee handling, gross/net status, denominator,
  lifecycle eligibility, and availability: Categories 2-10.
- Ticker/account/tag/rule/session/sequence/outcome/size and every other
  factual grouping or comparison dimension: Category 11.
- Equality, inequality, range, inclusion, exclusion, membership, text search,
  predicate precedence, and typed operand parsing: Category 12.
- Calendar/relative/trading/window/session resolution, event basis, timezone,
  and temporal endpoints: Category 13.
- Conversation-state selection, selected-object trust, pronoun resolution,
  slang, global ambiguity, response formatting, privacy/policy enforcement,
  causal conclusions, recommendation, prediction, provider access, and
  runtime implementation: Categories 15-20 and their later implementation
  contracts.

## Cross-Category References

- Category 1 provides `compare_groups`, `rank_results`, descriptive-result,
  clarification, and protected-action boundaries. Category 14 never turns a
  comparison into explanation, advice, prediction, or a write.
- Categories 2-10 supply metric meaning, valid result units, gross/net/fee
  handling, denominator, lifecycle eligibility, and missing-data behavior.
  A rank or comparison cannot alter any of those contracts.
- Category 11 supplies the server-authorized account scope, factual candidate
  fields, grouping dimensions, and coverage. It alone determines whether a
  named ticker/tag/rule/session/trade is factual and selectable.
- Category 12 validates typed filters and exclusions before composition.
- Category 13 resolves each requested period/window and its event/timezone
  contract. Category 14 may compare two already resolved compatible periods;
  it never invents `current`, `previous`, or a time baseline.

# 3. Planning Analysis

## 3.1 Required Planning Questions

1. **What exact problem does this category solve?** It maps the 29 source-order
   comparison/ranking expressions to a composition request without silently
   choosing a metric, group, comparator, baseline, direction, limit, tie rule,
   population, currency, fee basis, event, or time range.
2. **What canonical concepts belong here?** Only the thirteen Section 26
   ranking terms, fifteen Section 27 comparative forms, and one Section 28
   superlative/extremum family in Section 4.
3. **What related concepts belong elsewhere?** Intent is Category 1; metrics
   and formula/eligibility are Categories 2-10; dimensions and factual cohorts
   are Category 11; predicates are Category 12; temporal language is Category
   13; later context, slang, ambiguity, presentation, and policy remain
   Categories 15-20.
4. **What data is required?** One server-authorized user/workspace/account
   scope; accepted current facts; one known metric/result contract; candidate
   group definitions; compatible population/partition, unit, currency,
   gross/net/fee, lifecycle, time/event, and coverage contracts; and exact
   unrounded result values and counts.
5. **Which deterministic tools will answer requests?** A future read-only
   validator/aggregation service may compare or order a query already
   authorized and validated by the owning contracts. This draft authorizes no
   tool, parser, query, or execution.
6. **Which concepts are directly observed?** Accepted group labels/field values
   and stored result facts may be observed only inside server-authorized scope.
   The comparison/rank relation itself is not a raw Journal fact.
7. **Which concepts are deterministically derived?** Exact sort order,
   extremum, absolute difference, valid relative/percentage change,
   percentile, and baseline comparison are derived only from compatible
   declared values, populations, and denominator/tie contracts.
8. **Which concepts are proxy indicators?** `best`, `consistent`, `better`,
   `improved`, and `declined` are not self-proving quality, cause, or future
   performance. They require an explicit approved metric/balanced-score
   contract or clarification; no proxy becomes a causal or advisory claim.
9. **Which concepts are user-labelled?** A selected comparison target,
   approved tag/rule/setup label, saved baseline, or response preference can
   be used only when it is an authorized, typed, existing input under its
   owner. It is never inferred from prose or raw/private material.
10. **Which concepts are not measurable?** An unknown metric, missing or
    incompatible group, undefined baseline, unavailable fee/currency/time
    basis, unsupported percentile, balanced score lacking approval, missing ranked
    dimension, no meaningful percentage denominator, or incomplete coverage
    returns clarification or unavailable coverage, never an invented zero,
    default group, or fabricated order.
11. **Which terms are ambiguous?** `best`, `worst`, `biggest`, `smallest`,
    `consistent`, `more profitable`, `larger losses`, `current`, `previous`,
    `similar`, `all other`, `followed`, `broke`, `top`, `bottom`, `N`,
    percentile, `better`, `improved`, `declined`, and any omitted metric,
    grouping, target, period, baseline, direction, or eligible population.
12. **What defaults are safe?** Preserve the explicit metric and all owning
    contracts. An explicit `highest`/`most` maps to descending and an explicit
    `lowest`/`least` maps to ascending only after the metric and compatible
    population are known. No default exists for `best`/`worst`, balanced score,
    metric, group, comparison target, baseline, period, N/limit, percentile,
    denominator, fee mode, currency conversion, time/event basis, or a
    no-selection request. A deterministic tie policy must be declared by the
    eventual result contract, not guessed here.
13. **What conditions require clarification?** Ask one focused question when
    the highest-impact missing field is metric/basis; then group or baseline;
    then period/population; then direction/limit/percentile/denominator. Ask
    immediately when `best`/`worst` lacks an approved scoring rule, a relative
    claim lacks a valid baseline/denominator, `top`/`bottom` lacks a finite
    N, a selected comparison lacks trusted selected context, or candidates are
    not demonstrably compatible.
14. **What combinations are invalid?** Comparing different accounts or
    unauthorized scopes; mixing incompatible metric definitions, units,
    gross/net/fee states, currencies without approved conversion, time/event
    bases, lifecycle populations, or coverage; ranking raw/private identifiers;
    silently treating a missing group as zero; percentage change over zero or
    an undefined denominator; top/bottom with no limit; percentile without an
    approved population/method; choosing `best` by a hidden score; tie-breaking
    by raw IDs; and translating association/rank into motive, causation,
    prediction, recommendation, or a protected action.
15. **What evaluation coverage proves completion?** Later Sections 5-8 must
    cover all 29 records with explicit metric/basis, direction, compatible
    populations and partitions, gross/net/fee/currency/time/event contracts,
    top/bottom-N, extrema, relative/baseline/percentage/percentile cases,
    deterministic ties, no-selection and trusted-selection behavior,
    clarification, unavailable coverage, authorization/privacy, and
    cross-category metric/dimension/operator/temporal cases.

## 3.2 Dependencies

- **Locked language dependencies:** Category 1 supplies intent and safety
  boundary; Categories 2-10 supply deterministic metric contracts; Category
  11 supplies dimensions, server-authorized scope, and coverage; Category 12
  supplies predicates; and Category 13 supplies resolved temporal inputs.
- **Journal/module contracts:** accepted current facts/provenance; one
  server-authorized user/workspace/account scope; selected metric and grouping
  query contracts; explicit compatible partitions for units/currency/fee/time;
  visible `ready_closed`, `legitimate_open`, `needs_decision`, partial, and
  unavailable coverage; exact values/counts; and a future result contract that
  declares ordering, ties, finite limits, and redaction.
- **Future dependencies:** Categories 15-17 must later govern trusted
  conversational/selected context, trader terminology, and ambiguity recovery;
  Category 18 may format but cannot alter a result; Category 19 must enforce
  privacy, account isolation, evidence, causation, advice, and policy; and
  Category 20 must provide cross-category proof.
- **Unsupported dependencies:** browser/prose-derived selections; cross-account
  joins; raw account/source/broker identifiers; guessed cohorts, baseline,
  calendar, conversion, denominator, balanced score, tie order, N, percentile
  method, data value, or missing-state fallback; V3 fallback; provider calls;
  mutations; and model-created metrics/dimensions/tools.

## 3.3 Risks, Overlaps, and Decisions

| Area | Draft decision / risk control |
|---|---|
| Source preservation | Preserve exactly 13 Section 26 terms, 15 Section 27 forms, and one Section 28 declared family in their source order. Section 28 examples are later language material, not extra inventory records. |
| Metric and basis | Every composition names/retains one approved metric or an explicitly approved multi-metric score. Metric formula, units, gross/net/fee state, denominator, lifecycle eligibility, and coverage remain owned by the metric category. |
| Compatible population | Compare only the same compatible authorized population definition or an explicitly declared compatible partition. Return each group's exact definition, count, inclusion/exclusion, and coverage; do not mix account, currency, timezone/event, lifecycle, or fee states. |
| Currency and fees | Money comparisons/rankings retain recorded-currency partition and the metric's gross/net/fee contract. No implicit FX conversion, net-to-gross substitute, incomplete-fee default, or cross-currency total/rank is allowed. |
| Comparison output | Return values, exact units, absolute difference, percentage difference only where meaningful, counts, coverage, and limitations. Difference is descriptive only; it never proves cause, quality, or future outcome. |
| Relative and baseline | `improved`, `declined`, relative difference, and baseline language require an explicit compatible baseline and valid denominator. A zero/undefined baseline reports unavailable/undefined percentage rather than infinity, zero, or an invented interpretation. |
| Ranking and extrema | A superlative resolves to an approved metric plus explicit direction and finite result limit. `highest`/`most` and `lowest`/`least` may supply direction after metric/population resolution; `best`/`worst` need an explicit metric or approved score. |
| Top, bottom, N, and percentile | `top`/`bottom` require finite N; no N means clarification unless a trusted prior result supplies it. Percentile requires an approved compatible population, method, boundary, and tie treatment. Ranking never substitutes a record-count window or a time range. |
| Deterministic order and ties | Sort uses exact unrounded valid values. The future result contract must state a stable privacy-safe secondary order and tie display rule. Do not break ties with raw/internal/source IDs, arbitrary row order, or a silent rounding difference. |
| Selection and context | A selected trade/ticker/group/baseline may be used only when a later context contract supplies a trusted authorized typed selection. With no selected entity, do not choose one from visible prose/UI; clarify the target or use an explicit named authorized target. |
| Grouping and operators | Category 11 owns groups and Category 12 owns filters/exclusions. This category requires already valid inputs and never treats a rank order as a predicate, creates an `all other` cohort without a defined complement, or changes filter precedence. |
| Coverage and sample size | Empty/partial/unavailable, open, and decision-bound coverage remain visible. Do not rank absent groups, represent omitted coverage as zero, or call a small sample reliable; the eventual metric/result contract controls thresholds and limitations. |
| Privacy and safety | Outputs are bounded, redacted, and account-isolated. No raw IDs, source text, broker/account identifiers, other-account results, motive, causation, prediction, financial advice, rule change, or write is permitted. |
| Category ownership | Category 14 owns only composition semantics. Category 1 owns intent; Categories 2-10 metrics; Category 11 dimensions/cohorts; Category 12 operators; Category 13 time; and Categories 15-20 later context/policy/evaluation. |

## Proposed Inventory Additions

None. `top N`, `bottom N`, percentile, relative/percentage difference,
baseline, tie handling, finite limit, selected/no-selection, sort direction,
and absolute difference are required shared composition semantics. They are not
extra source-plan canonical records without controller approval.

## Proposed Removals or Merges

None. Source terms overlap conversationally but remain separate in Version 1.
Their eventual registry entries must distinguish explicit metric, direction,
baseline, sign/absolute-value, population, denominator, and coverage behavior
without silently collapsing `best` into `most profitable`, `biggest` into
`largest losses`, or `current versus previous` into `before versus after`.

## `best`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Inventory ID | C14-RK-001 |
| Category | Comparison and Ranking Language |
| Subcategory | Ranking term |
| Canonical name | best |
| Display name | Best |
| Exact definition | Compose a bounded ranking request described as `best` only when the user or a separately approved contract supplies the ranking metric or documented balanced-score definition, that metric/score contract declares the ranking direction, an authorized compatible population/grouping, a finite positive integer result limit N, and a deterministic tie rule. Missing, zero, negative, or fractional N is invalid and requires clarification. A loss metric must explicitly declare whether its signed or absolute-loss ordering represents the requested meaning; `best` never infers that direction. It does not itself define quality, a metric, a score, a baseline, a time range, a group, or advice. |
| Distinction from related concepts | It is an underspecified superlative that requires an explicit metric or approved score with declared direction and positive-integer N; it is not automatically `most_profitable`, `highest_win_rate`, `most_consistent`, `top`, `worst`, a loss ordering, a causal explanation, or a recommendation. |
| Evidence classification | Deterministically derived only from already validated, authorized, compatible grouped metric results and a declared ranking/score direction, finite positive integer N, and tie contract; no direct Journal fact is named by this word alone. |
| Capability status | Planned |
| Result units | The exact units, gross/net/fee state, recorded-currency partition or separately approved conversion contract, event/time basis, population/group definition, declared sort direction, unrounded sort value, requested/returned finite positive integer N, tie treatment, counts, coverage, and limitations of the selected metric/score; never a generic quality unit. |
| Open-trade support | Only if the explicitly selected metric and population contract admit the relevant open lifecycle. Open, `needs_decision`, partial, and unavailable coverage remain separate and never become ranked completed evidence by this term. |
| Fee handling | No fee default. A money metric retains its owning gross/before-fee or net/after-fee definition, charge coverage, currency partition, and limitations; an incomplete-fee result cannot silently stand in for a fee-complete result. |
| Version | 1 |

## `best` Language Registry

### Exact Definition
Compose a `best` ranking only after an explicit metric or approved score declares direction, compatible authorized population/group, positive integer N, and privacy-safe ties.
### Formal Wording
- “Rank the approved groups by the declared best-score contract.”
### Normal Conversational Wording
- “Which group did best by the metric I picked?”
### Trader Slang
- “What was my best bucket?”
### Abbreviations
- “Best WR grp?”
### Common Misspellings
- “Which one was my beest group?”
### Noisy or Incomplete Input
- “best group?”
### Singular and Plural Forms
- “Best result” / “best results.”
### Full Questions
- “Which authorized ticker group is best by the selected metric?”
### Commands
- “Show the best 3 approved groups by net P&L.”
### Sentence Fragments
- “Best eligible group.”
### Follow-Up Wording
- “Use that same approved score for the best groups.”
### Correction Wording
- “I meant best by fee-complete net P&L, not by win rate.”
### Comparison Wording
- “Compare the best group with the explicit baseline.”
### Ranking Wording
- “Rank the best 5 groups under the approved score.”
### Negated Wording
- “Not the best by a hidden score.”
### Exclusion Wording
- “Show best groups excluding the authorized selected ticker.”
### Multi-Filter Wording
- “Best 3 long-trade ticker groups in the resolved period.”
### Multi-Part Question Wording
- “Show the best 3 groups and include counts and coverage.”
### Ambiguous Wording
- “What did I trade best?”
### Negative Examples
These examples must not map to this concept.
- “Give me the best trade to take tomorrow.”
### Context Requirements
Trusted metric/approved-score, authorized scope, declared direction, group/population, period/event basis, positive N, and tie contract.
### Required Data
- Exact metric/score formula, units, gross/net/fee/currency partition where relevant, exact values, counts, coverage, and tie rule.
### Optional Data
- Trusted prior metric/group/period context and privacy-safe display labels.
### Valid Filters
- Only Category 11 fields and Category 12 predicates already authorized and compatible.
### Valid Groupings
- One explicitly selected compatible Category 11 grouping.
### Valid Operators
- `rank_results`; declared score direction; finite positive integer N; deterministic tie rule.
### Compatible Intents
- `rank_results`, `calculate_metric`, `group_and_aggregate`, `compare_groups`.
### Incompatible Combinations
- Hidden score/direction, cross-account groups, raw IDs, zero/negative/fractional N, incompatible currency/fee/time/lifecycle partitions, cause, advice, or writes.
### Default Interpretation
No default metric, score, direction, group, period, baseline, fee basis, currency conversion, or N.
### Clarification Conditions
Clarify one unresolved highest-impact field: metric/approved score, then direction, group/population, then N.
### Recommended Clarification Wording
- “Which metric or approved score should define ‘best’?”
### Unsupported Conditions
- Missing approved score/direction, incompatible population, unavailable metric coverage, or unimplemented ranking contract.
### Target Analytics Tool or Query Capability
- Future validated read-only `rank_results` over an authorized grouped metric result.
### Result Units
- Exact selected metric units/basis, direction, N, unrounded values, privacy-safe ties, counts, coverage, and limitations; never raw identifiers.
### Fee Handling
- No default; preserve the selected metric’s gross/net, fee coverage, and compatible currency contract.
### Open-Trade Handling
- Only owning metric eligibility applies; open/decision/partial states remain visible coverage.
### Sample-Size Considerations
- Report every group count and limitation; `best` never makes a small sample reliable.

For loss/P&L only, next clarify gross/before-fee versus fee-complete-net and signed/absolute representation. Then clarify applicable currency/fee coverage, group/population/time, and finally N.

### Fee Handling
- A direct fee/cost metric retains its own declared nonnegative representation and fee coverage. A selected loss/P&L metric must retain selected gross/before-fee or fee-complete-net basis and applicable fee completeness; never infer, substitute, or omit fees.
### Open-Trade Handling
- Only the owning selected metric’s eligibility applies; open and decision-bound states remain coverage and are never silently treated as closed loss.
### Sample-Size Considerations
- Report group counts, selected-basis values, fee/currency coverage, N, ties, and limitations; rank is descriptive, not cause or advice.

### Open-Trade Handling
- Selected trade and peer population each retain metric eligibility; open and decision-bound states remain coverage.

- Report peer count, representation/grain, selection and coverage limitations; comparison is not causation, quality, or advice.

## `one_ticker_versus_all_other_tickers` Language Registry
### Exact Definition
- Compare an explicit authorized left ticker population with an explicit authorized right complement of all other eligible tickers under declared universe/complement semantics, compatible metric/basis/units/time/population/fee/currency coverage, and fixed no-measured-difference equality outcome. Percentage needs separate explicit baseline and validated denominator; the complement is never implicit baseline.
### Formal Wording
- “Compare the authorized ticker with its defined eligible-ticker complement.”
### Normal Conversational Wording
- “How did this authorized ticker compare with all other eligible tickers?”
### Trader Slang
- “How did this name stack up against the rest?”
### Abbreviations
- “Ticker vs others?”
### Common Misspellings
- “Ticker versus all othr tickers?”
### Noisy or Incomplete Input
- “this ticker vs rest?”
### Singular and Plural Forms

### Full Questions
- “Compare authorized ticker A with the defined complement of all other eligible tickers by selected net P/L.”
### Commands
- “Compare the named authorized ticker with its eligible complement.”
### Sentence Fragments
- “This ticker versus all others.”
### Follow-Up Wording
- “Keep the same ticker universe and complement.”
### Correction Wording
- “Use the eligible-ticker complement, not all raw tickers.”
### Comparison Wording
- “Show the ticker and complement values without treating complement as percentage baseline.”
### Ranking Wording
- “Rank eligible tickers by the same metric instead.”
### Negated Wording
- “Not an inferred ticker or undefined all-other group.”
### Exclusion Wording
- “Exclude the authorized selected tag from ticker and complement.”
### Multi-Filter Wording
- “Compare ticker A with all other eligible long-trade tickers in the resolved period.”
### Multi-Part Question Wording
- “Show ticker, universe/complement contract, both values, difference, no-measured-difference result, counts, coverage, and percentage only if validated.”
### Ambiguous Wording
- “How did this ticker do versus the rest?”
### Negative Examples
These examples must not map to this concept.
- “Which ticker should I trade instead?”
### Context Requirements
- Trusted authorized ticker, eligible universe/complement contract, compatible metric/basis/units/time/population/fee/currency coverage, fixed equality, and optional separate percentage baseline.
### Required Data
- Authorized ticker display handle, universe/complement definition, side values, metric/basis/units/time, coverage, fixed equality, counts, and percentage data only if requested.
### Optional Data
- Trusted prior ticker context and privacy-safe labels.
### Valid Filters
- Authorized compatible filters applied under declared eligible-universe and complement semantics.
### Valid Groupings
- One authorized left ticker and one explicit right all-other eligible-ticker complement.
### Valid Operators
- Read-only `compare_groups`; declared difference; fixed no-measured-difference outcome; percentage only with separate explicit baseline and validated denominator.
### Compatible Intents
- Locked Category 1 `compare_groups`, `calculate_metric`, and `group_and_aggregate` intents only.
### Incompatible Combinations
- Missing/unauthorized ticker, undefined universe/complement, raw IDs, incompatible metric/basis/time/population/fee/currency, complement as implicit baseline, equality outcome other than no measured difference, or cause/advice claims.
### Default Interpretation
- No default ticker, universe, complement, metric/basis, period, population, percentage baseline, or denominator; equal values report no measured difference.
### Clarification Conditions
- Clarify authorized ticker, eligible universe/complement, metric/basis, time/population, applicable fee/currency, then separate percentage baseline only if requested. Equality needs no clarification; validated data decides percentage availability.
### Recommended Clarification Wording

- “Which eligible ticker universe should define all other tickers?”

## `tagged_versus_untagged` Language Registry

## `superlative_and_extremum_questions` Language Registry
### Exact Definition
- Compose a bounded extremum/superlative ranking only after explicit eligible metric or approved score, declared direction, compatible population/group/time/basis/fee/currency coverage, finite positive integer N, exact unrounded sort values, and deterministic privacy-safe ties resolve. One extremum uses N=1; no metric, direction, N, tie policy, cause, or advice is defaulted.
### Formal Wording
- “Return the declared extremum under the explicit metric, direction, and result limit.”
### Normal Conversational Wording
- “What is the top or bottom authorized result by the selected measure?”
### Trader Slang
- “What was my number-one bucket by the selected metric?”
### Abbreviations
- “Top N?”
### Common Misspellings
- “Suprlative result?”
### Noisy or Incomplete Input
- “my best?”
### Singular and Plural Forms
- “Extremum” / “extrema.”
### Full Questions
- “Show the top 3 authorized setup groups by selected net P/L with unrounded ties handled by the approved rule.”
### Commands
- “Return the bottom 5 groups by the selected metric.”
### Sentence Fragments
- “Best result.”
### Follow-Up Wording
- “Keep the same metric, direction, N, and tie policy.”
### Correction Wording
- “Use lowest expectancy, not a hidden best score.”
### Comparison Wording
- “Compare the extremum with an explicit compatible baseline.”
### Ranking Wording
- “Rank the top 3 by the declared descending direction.”
### Negated Wording
- “Not best by an assumed quality score.”
### Exclusion Wording
- “Exclude the authorized selected tag from the ranking.”
### Multi-Filter Wording
- “Show the top 3 long-trade ticker groups in the resolved period by selected metric.”
### Multi-Part Question Wording
- “Return N, metric, direction, exact unrounded values, deterministic ties, counts, coverage, and limitations.”
### Ambiguous Wording
- “What was my best?”
### Negative Examples
These examples must not map to this concept.
- “Tell me which trade will be best next week.”
### Context Requirements
- Trusted metric/score, direction, authorized population/group/time/basis/fee/currency contract, finite positive integer N, exact unrounded values, and deterministic privacy-safe tie policy.
### Required Data
- Metric/version/units/representation/direction, population/group/time/basis coverage, positive N, exact unrounded values, tie policy, counts, and limitations.
### Optional Data
- Trusted prior metric/filter/group context and privacy-safe labels.
### Valid Filters
- Authorized compatible dimensions/predicates preserving selected metric contract.
### Valid Groupings
- One explicit compatible Category 11 grouping or declared result population.
### Valid Operators
- Read-only `rank_results`; declared direction; finite positive integer N; exact unrounded sort values; deterministic privacy-safe tie rule.
### Compatible Intents
- Locked Category 1 `rank_results`, `calculate_metric`, `group_and_aggregate`, and `compare_groups` intents only.
### Incompatible Combinations
- Missing metric/direction/N/tie policy, zero/negative/fractional N, rounded-value tie break, raw IDs, incompatible basis/population/time/fee/currency, hidden quality score, cause/advice/prediction/writes.
### Default Interpretation
- No default metric, score, direction, group, period, basis, currency conversion, N, or tie rule.
### Clarification Conditions
- Clarify metric/score, declared direction, grouping/population, period/basis/fee/currency, positive integer N, then deterministic tie policy.
### Recommended Clarification Wording
- “Which eligible metric or approved score should rank the results?”
- “Which declared direction should apply?”
- “Which authorized grouping or population should rank?”
- “Which compatible period should apply?”
- “Which metric basis should apply?”
- “Which applicable gross/net/fee/currency contract should apply?”
- “What positive integer N should I return?”
- “Which deterministic privacy-safe tie policy should apply?”
### Unsupported Conditions
- Missing/incompatible metric/direction/population/basis/N/tie policy or no ranking capability.
### Target Analytics Tool or Query Capability
- Future validated read-only `rank_results` over exact compatible metric/score results.
### Result Units
- Ordered privacy-safe rows with metric/score units/representation/direction, population/time/basis/fee/currency state, requested/returned N, exact unrounded values, deterministic ties, counts, coverage, and limitations; never raw IDs.
### Fee Handling
- No default; money metric/score retains exact selected gross/net/fee and compatible currency partition.
### Open-Trade Handling
- Only selected metric eligibility applies; open and decision-bound coverage remains visible.
### Sample-Size Considerations
- Report requested/returned N, ties, counts, coverage, and limitations; rank is descriptive, not quality or advice.

**C14-E29 resolved-case metric invariant:** In every resolved supported case
below, the canonical `net_pnl` token means the locked owner formula: sum each
eligible `ready_closed` round trip's gross P/L minus allocated `charge_cost`
plus allocated `charge_credit` within the authorized group, using conserving
allocation and one compatible fee-complete USD partition. Every result is
ordered by that exact unrounded group total and displays total net P/L in USD
under the owner metric presentation contract; abbreviated references such as
"locked formula" never weaken or replace this exact definition. Empty,
fee-incomplete, mixed-currency, partial, or unavailable groups are not zeroed,
estimated, silently omitted, or ranked as comparable, and their counts and
limitations remain visible.

evaluation/coverage result is PASS. All substantive planning, canonical,

complete. Every ranking and comparison case preserves its explicit
metric/formula, case-declared direction, population or group, period, basis,

defaults.

Batch 9 remediation invariants apply to every resolved case in the three
arrays. `C14-E25` uses the locked `median_net_pnl_per_trade` owner: sort exact
`net_pnl` values for eligible fee-covered `ready_closed` peers, take the odd
middle value or the exact arithmetic mean of the two middle exact values for
even N, and require peer N greater than zero. Empty peers make the median and
direct comparison unavailable, never zero. For resolved total-net-P/L cases
in `C14-E26` and `C14-E27`, if either side has no eligible fee-covered
`ready_closed` trades, that side's value and the direct comparison are
empty/unavailable, never fabricated zero; incomplete or fee-incomplete
coverage stays partial or unavailable with side counts and coverage visible.

Final Batch 10 preserves the remaining owner contracts. `C14-E28` requires an
authorized saved rule/version plus deterministic applicability, followed,
broke, excluded, and unassessable evidence; it never infers status from notes,
outcomes, or behavior. Its locked total `net_pnl` comparison uses compatible
side-specific fee-complete currency populations, signed followed-minus-broke
difference plus magnitude, fixed no-measured-difference equality, visible
samples/coverage, and a separately explicit meaningful non-zero baseline only
when percentage is requested. `C14-E29` requires an explicit metric/formula,
declared direction, compatible authorized population/group/time/basis/fee/
currency coverage, finite positive integer N, exact unrounded sort key, and a
trusted approved deterministic privacy-safe tie rule while displaying the
